coverageLabel: 120-credit draft with published transfer choices; unresolved requirements are flagged
ledgerExplanation: 39 unique general-education credits + 45 major/foundation credits + 36 free-elective credits = 120. GOVT 220 also satisfies cultural studies, with its three credits counted once. The baseline retains three credits for UNIV 104 instead of assuming an exemption. Transfer-triggered religion waivers are retained for individual review.

obligations.title: Official transfer evaluation
obligations.notes: Submit official transcripts and obtain written confirmation of individual applicability and any required approval for future outside courses. Published awards are not individual approvals.

obligations.title: Graduation eligibility
obligations.notes: Confirm the 2026–27 catalog applies, 2.0 overall GPA, C or higher in all major courses, all prerequisites, major residency and graduation application.

obligations.title: Course calendar
obligations.notes: CJUS 420 is listed for fall semester. Verify actual delivery, prerequisite completion and transcript deadlines before making a final schedule.

rulesNotes: This is the general Criminal Justice program for the selected delivery format. Concentrations have different requirements and must not inherit this ledger without review.

At least 30 credits must be earned through Liberty and at least 30 must be upper level. The 90-credit outside maximum is a ceiling, not a claim that this draft identifies 90 applicable outside credits.

The catalog requires 25% of the major at Liberty. This model conservatively uses all 45 foundation/core hours and reserves 12 hours rounded to three-credit courses; Liberty must confirm its exact major-residency denominator.
GOVT 220 fills both the foundation requirement and cultural studies; it is one course and three credits, never six. GOVT 200 is not reused for critical thinking.
Receiving Liberty course level controls upper-level counting. A source course with an advanced number does not itself establish an upper-level award.
Options within a requirement are alternatives; choosing multiple alternatives does not create extra applicable credits.
Approved transfer totals of 45 may waive RLGN 104; approved totals of 60 may also waive THEO 104. Waivers are not automatic and award no credit.
If Liberty approves a requirement waiver or technology/UNIV exemption, add nonduplicating degree-applicable elective credit to preserve 120 hours. This baseline does not apply those waivers.
Outside mappings not found for exact major requirements remain research gaps. Their university fallbacks do not establish that Liberty requires those courses in residence.

University major prerequisite pairs are modeled; other university elective/general-education prerequisites, provider prerequisites and actual course offerings require review. No finish date is verified.
unresolved: Obtain Liberty’s individual evaluation of all prior and planned credit, including duplicate-learning decisions, source versions/recommendation windows, and exact major-residency calculation.
Research additional outside awards for the exact unmapped major and general-education requirements. University fallback rows are not proof that outside credit is disallowed.
Confirm transfer-triggered religion waivers and technology/UNIV exemptions. Any waived hours need nonduplicating replacement electives to maintain 120 total credits.
Verify remaining university/provider prerequisites and term availability; CJUS 420 is listed for fall. No executable term-by-term graduation schedule is established.
